linkedin.title: Personalized news is currently broken, but it is about to get much better.
linkedin.body:
Most news feeds today are built to keep you scrolling rather than to keep you informed. They prioritize outrage and volume because that is what their algorithms are trained to optimize for. We think that is the wrong approach to staying connected to the world.

At Headlinne, we are mapping out a different path. The future of news isn't about feeding you more content. It is about distilling the noise so you can actually understand the stories that matter to you. We are moving toward a model where your news feed acts more like a personal editor than a firehose of headlines.

This means building systems that respect your time. It means surfacing the context behind a story so you don't have to jump between five different tabs to get the full picture. True personalization should make you smarter, not just keep you occupied. We are currently building the tools to make that kind of clarity the new standard for how we consume information.

instagram.caption:
AMD is making a massive bet on the future of artificial intelligence by acquiring World Labs.

The deal is valued at over $8 billion, a huge sum for a company that has only existed for less than a year.

World Labs was co-founded by Dr. Fei-Fei Li, who is widely considered a giant in the field of AI research. Her leadership helped the startup skyrocket to a billion-dollar valuation almost immediately after launching.

This move signals that AMD is looking to aggressively compete in the rapidly changing AI market. It is a clear sign that they are prioritizing top-tier research talent to drive their future products.

story_card.standfirst: Scientists have found a potential chink in the armor of bacteria that can survive almost

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers are studying bacterial spores, which are survival capsules designed to endure anything.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Bacteria create these spores by drying out and wrapping themselves in tough protein armor.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: These spores resist boiling, radiation, and space travel. They can even invade hospital environments.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: New research into their energy budgets could reveal how to finally break their hibernation cycle.

story_card.caption:
Scientists are investigating how hibernating bacteria spores survive extreme conditions like space and boiling.

These spores act like a survival capsule, shutting down chemical processes to stay alive when environments turn hostile. By studying their energy usage, researchers hope to find a way to stop these germs from invading hospitals.
